content: 1. Ethylene oxide gas sterilizers have been extensively studied for their role in infection control and hospital epidemiology, as documented in a 1996 publication in Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology (Volume 17, Issue 2, Pages 92–100). 2. A controlled, multifactorial investigation into the antimicrobial efficacy of endoscopic disinfection procedures was conducted by Cronmiller JR, Nelson DK, Salman G, and colleagues, with findings published in Gastrointestinal Endoscopy in 1999 (Volume 50, Issue 2, Pages 152–158). 3. Nystrom B explored the disinfection of surgical instruments, with results published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 1981 (Volume 2, Issue 4, Pages 363–368). 4. Parker HH and Johnson RB evaluated the effectiveness of ethylene oxide in sterilizing dental handpieces, as reported in the Journal of Dentistry in 1995 (Volume 23, Issue 2, Pages 113–115). 5. Kampf G, Bloss R, and Martiny H investigated the fixation of dried blood on surfaces using glutaraldehyde and peracetic acid, with their findings published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 2004 (Volume 57, Issue 2, Pages 139–143). 6. Rutala WA, Gergen MF, and Jones JF, among others, assessed microbial contamination levels on surgical instruments, with their study accessible via PubMed (PMID: 9584809). 7. Pittet D, Allegranzi B, Sax H, and colleagues developed an evidence-based model for hand transmission during patient care and emphasized the importance of improved practices, as published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2006 (Volume 6, Issue 10, Pages 641–652). 8. The World Health Organization (WHO) released advanced draft guidelines on hand hygiene in healthcare settings, which are available online. 9. Collins CH and Grange JM reviewed tuberculosis transmission in laboratories and necropsy rooms, with their findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 10491868). 10. Marris E reported on the challenges faced by Marburg workers in gaining the trust of local communities, with the study available via PubMed (PMID: 15846312). 11. Claydon SM discussed the risks associated with high-risk autopsies and the necessary protective measures, as detailed in the American Journal of Forensic Medicine and Pathology in 1993 (Volume 14, Issue 3, Pages 253–256). 12. Li L, Gu J, Shi X, and colleagues outlined the principles, practices, and future prospects of biosafety level 3 laboratories for autopsies of patients with severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2005 (Volume 41, Issue 6, Pages 815–821). 13. Nolte KB, Taylor DG, and Richmond JY examined biosafety considerations for autopsies, with their findings published in the American Journal of Forensic Medicine and Pathology in 2002 (Volume 23, Issue 2, Pages 107–122). 14. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) provided infection control guidelines for healthcare, home, and community settings during the SARS outbreak, with specific recommendations for laboratory and pathology procedures available online. 15. The Royal College of Pathologists issued guidelines on autopsy practices, which are detailed in a report by their working group. 16. Burton J and Rutty GN discussed the design and construction of autopsy suites in their book The Hospital Autopsy, published by Arnold in 2001 (Pages 37–41). 17. Healing TD, Hoffman PN, and Young SE reviewed the infection hazards associated with human cadavers in a 1995 issue of the Communicable Disease Report (Volume 5, Issue 5, Pages R61–68). 18. Newsom SW, Rowlands C, and Matthews J investigated aerosol generation in mortuaries, with their findings published in the Journal of Clinical Pathology in 1983 (Volume 36, Issue 2, Pages 127–132). 19. Kantor HS, Poblete R, and Pusateri SL reported on nosocomial tuberculosis transmission from unsuspected cases, with their study accessible via PubMed (PMID: 3364442). 20. Al-Wali W, Kibbler CC, and McLaughlin JE evaluated the bacteriological performance of a downdraft necropsy ventilation system, with findings available via PubMed (PMID: 8408701). 21. Foldy SL, Barthell E, and Silva J, among others, described the SARS Surveillance Project, an internet-enabled multiregion surveillance system for emerging diseases, with their study accessible via PubMed (PMID: 15717395). 22. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a checklist for influenza pandemic preparedness planning, which is available as a downloadable PDF. 23. Harper SA, Fukuda K, Uyeki TM, and colleagues provided recommendations for the prevention and control of influenza, as outlined by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), with their report accessible via PubMed (PMID: 16086456). 24. Hehme N, Engelmann H, Kunzel W, and colleagues shared lessons learned from H2N2 and H9N2 candidate vaccines in a study accessible via PubMed (PMID: 12458361). 25. Jefferson T, Demicheli V, and Di Pietrantonj C reviewed the efficacy of amantadine and rimantadine for influenza A in adults, with their findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 16625539). 26. Bhat N, Wright JG, Broder KR, and colleagues analyzed influenza-associated deaths among children in the United States during 2003–2004, with their study accessible via PubMed (PMID: 16354892). 27. Aiello AE, Coulborn RM, Aragon TJ, and colleagues identified gaps in research on nonpharmaceutical interventions for pandemic influenza, as published in the American Journal of Infection Control in 2010 (Volume 38, Issue 4, Pages 251–258). 28. Lee K conducted a systematic review on physical interventions to reduce respiratory virus transmission, with resource use implications detailed in a publication available online. 29. Pippin DJ, Verderame RA, and Weber KK evaluated the efficacy of face masks in preventing inhalation of airborne contaminants, as published in the Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery in 1987 (Volume 45, Issue 4, Pages 319–323). 30. Kaye K, Weber D, and Rutala W discussed nosocomial infections associated with respiratory therapy in the third edition of Hospital Epidemiology and Infection Control, published by Lippincott Williams & Wilkins in 2004 (Pages 1207–1222). 31. Derrick JL and Gomersall CD assessed the filtration capacity of multiple surgical masks in protecting healthcare staff from SARS, as published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 2005 (Volume 59, Issue 4, Pages 365–368). 32. Lenhart SW, Seitz T, Trout D, and colleagues reviewed issues affecting respirator selection for workers exposed to infectious aerosols, with a focus on healthcare settings, as published in Applied Biosafety in 2004 (Volume 9, Issue 1, Pages 20–36). 33. The World Health Organization (WHO) released a practical guide for the prevention of hospital-acquired infections, available as a downloadable PDF. 34. Brady MT, Evans J, and Cuartas J studied the survival and disinfection of parainfluenza viruses on environmental surfaces, as published in the American Journal of Infection Control in 1990 (Volume 18, Issue 1, Pages 18–23). 35. Suarez DL, Spackman E, and Senne DA, among others, evaluated the impact of various disinfectants on the detection of avian influenza virus using real-time RT-PCR, as published in Avian Diseases in 2003 (Volume 47, Supplement 3, Pages 1091–1095). 36. Sattar SA, Jacobsen H, Springthorpe VS, and colleagues investigated chemical disinfection to interrupt rhinovirus transfer from surfaces to hands, as published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology in 1993 (Volume 59, Issue 5, Pages 1579–1585). 37. Rabeneau HF, Kampf G, Cinatl J, and colleagues evaluated the efficacy of various disinfectants against SARS coronavirus, as published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 2005 (Volume 61, Issue 2, Pages 107–111). 38. Dettenkofer M, Wenzler S, Amthor S, and colleagues conducted a systematic review on the influence of environmental surface disinfection on nosocomial infection rates, as published in the American Journal of Infection Control in 2004 (Volume 32, Issue 2, Pages 84–89). 39. Scott E and Bloomfield SF investigated the effectiveness of detergent washing, drying, and chemical disinfection on cleaning cloth contamination, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 2341327). 40. Medcraft JW, Hawkins JM, and Fletcher BN, among others, highlighted potential hazards from spray cleaning of hospital ward floors, with their study accessible via PubMed (PMID: 2883222). 41. Spaulding EH discussed chemical disinfection of medical and surgical materials in the book Disinfection, Sterilization, and Preservation, edited by Lawrence C and Block S, published by Lea & Febiger in 1968 (Pages 517–531). 42. Rutala WA provided guidelines for the selection and use of disinfectants in the American Journal of Infection Control in 1996 (Volume 24, Issue 4, Pages 313–342). 43. Cefai C, Richards J, Gould FK, and colleagues reported an outbreak of Acinetobacter respiratory tract infection due to incomplete disinfection of ventilatory equipment, as published in the Journal of Hospital Infection in 1990 (Volume 15, Issue 2, Pages 177–182). 44. Craven DE, Lichtenberg DA, Goulart TA, and colleagues identified contaminated medication nebulizers in mechanical ventilator circuits as a source of bacterial aerosols, as published in the American Journal of Medicine in 1984 (Volume 77, Issue 5, Pages 834–838). 45. Spach DH, Silverstein FE, and Stamm WE reviewed infection transmission via gastrointestinal endoscopy and bronchoscopy, with their findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 8416308). 46. Weber DJ and Rutala WA shared lessons from outbreaks associated with bronchoscopy, with their study accessible via PubMed (PMID: 11583206). 47. Wheeler PW, Lancaster D, and Kaiser AB investigated bronchopulmonary cross-colonization and infection related to mycobacterial contamination of bronchoscope suction valves, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 2708844). 48. Poledore AP evaluated the sanitizing efficiency of dishwashing machines, as published in the Journal of Foodservice in 1980 (Pages 17–25). 49. Stahl Wernersson E, Johansson E, and Hakanson H studied cross-contamination in dishwashers, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 15066743). 50. Ijaz MK, Sattar SA, Johnson-Lussenburg CM, and colleagues examined the effects of relative humidity, atmospheric temperature, and suspending medium on the airborne survival of human rotavirus, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 3000566). 51. Marks PJ, Vipond IB, Carlisle D, and colleagues provided evidence for airborne transmission of Norwalk-like virus in a hotel restaurant, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 10982072). 52. Marks PJ, Vipond IB, Regan FM, and colleagues documented a school outbreak of Norwalk-like virus, providing evidence for airborne transmission, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 12948373). 53. Battles DR and Vesley D studied the relationship between wash water temperature and sanitation in hospital laundry, as published in the Journal of Environmental Health in 1981 (Volume 43, Issue 5, Pages 244–250). 54. Blaser MJ, Smith PF, Cody HJ, and colleagues investigated the killing of fabric-associated bacteria in hospital laundry using low-temperature washing, as published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1984 (Volume 149, Issue 1, Pages 48–57). 55. Christian RR, Manchester JT, and Mellor MT assessed the bacteriological quality of fabrics washed at lower-than-standard temperatures in a hospital laundry facility, as published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology in 1983 (Volume 45, Issue 2, Pages 591–597). 56. Barker J and Jones MV examined the potential spread of infection caused by aerosol contamination of surfaces after flushing a domestic toilet, as published in the Journal of Applied Microbiology in 2005 (Volume 99, Issue 2, Pages 339–347). 57. Morawska L explored the fate of droplets in indoor environments and the potential to prevent the spread of infection, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 16948710). 58. The Safe Injection Global Network (SIGN) Alliance provided resources on injection safety, available online. 59. Karanfil LV, Conlon M, Lykens K, and colleagues reported on reducing nosocomial transmission rates of respiratory syncytial virus, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 10196485). 60. Mlinaric-Galinovic G and Varda-Brkic D reviewed nosocomial respiratory syncytial virus infections in children's wards, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 10974574). 61. Thorburn K, Kerr S, Taylor N, and colleagues documented an RSV outbreak in a pediatric intensive care unit, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 15236847). 62. Ibricevic A, Pekosz A, Walter MJ, and colleagues studied influenza virus receptor specificity and cell tropism in mouse and human airway epithelial cells, with findings accessible via PubMed (PMID: 16840327). 63. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued guidelines for preventing the transmission of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in healthcare settings.
